scope: Review of the eleven completed follow-up cases (dossier, reading, separate review, previous review, mechanical corrections) against the existing ontology and the frozen pilot contract. Selected saved source files were re-read to check quotations that conclusions depend on. No new public sources were fetched. No case, pilot, ontology or production file was edited. Nothing here approves a historical person merge, identity, date or graph edge.

rules.title: Keep the parent named inside a name
rules.rule: Every 'bar/ben/b. R./son of X' inside a name creates a local parent entity and one child_of claim with basis name_internal. The parent does not need to speak or act. Scope the parent and the claim to the reading branch that has that name form. Keep all spellings of the parent's name on one parent entity when only the spelling varies; make separate parent entities when a variant changes the name. Never merge two parents because their names match. A repeated patronymic is more evidence for the same claim, not a new claim. Add an alternative 'fixed name or epithet' reading only when a source says so; a spelling difference alone does not.

rules.title: Keep printed and corrected kinship side by side, with unnamed links
rules.rule: When a family relation needs an unnamed person in the middle, create that local person and chain simple claims (child_of, sibling_of). Show the compound label (nephew, uncle) as a derived display, not a stored relation. When the printed text and a correction give different kinship, keep both as branches with their evidence types. A conflict between branches is conditional on an identity choice (for example, that two mentions are one person). Store it as a conditional constraint, never as a rule that deletes a branch. A preferred reading is a decision revision, not a property of the data.

rules.title: Give women and household members their own local entities
rules.rule: A woman or servant named only through another person (mother of, maidservant of the household of) gets her own local entity, labelled by the source words. Add one new predicate, member_of_household (person to household entity, subtype such as servant or attendant). Do not place the household head in the scene because the household is named. Record who supplies a family link: the passage, a commentary, a translator's gloss, or biblical background. Figures inside a quoted verse and hypothetical people in an unquoted part of a Mishnah are not participants.

rules.title: Keep speaker, addressee, target and content apart
rules.rule: A speech claim has separate roles: speaker, addressee, audience, target and content. Fill addressee only when the text marks it (to him, to them, before X) or the target clearly replies. A target can be a person, a statement or an explanation. If witnesses differ on the addressee or its number, make branches. An 'or some say to Y' addressee is one speech event with alternative addressees.

rules.title: Type the voice, including the anonymous discussion
rules.rule: Every claim records a voice kind: anonymous_discussion, unattributed_opinion (first opinion in a Mishnah or baraita), named_speaker, nested_quote, or later_author. A position label ('the one who says X') is a role reference to the owner of that position, not a new person. An answer built by the anonymous discussion on someone's behalf ('what does X do with it?', 'X needs it for') is that voice's reconstruction, not X's speech. An unattributed first opinion is not the group 'the Sages' unless the text says so. When the text does not mark where a speaker stops, make a speaker-boundary branch.

rules.title: Store negation, unsaid words, restriction and rhetoric inside their content
rules.rule: A statement about words that were not said is a statement node with negative polarity, used as evidence; it is not an utterance. 'Had he not heard what X said?' concerns knowledge of one teaching; it creates neither a contact edge nor a 'never met' edge. 'Not ... except' needs a scope field (only/except). Rhetorical versus plain readings, and negation that differs by edition, are branches on the content. An edition that lacks a word does not deny what the word says.

rules.title: Label every wording by what kind of evidence it is
rules.rule: Each wording used as evidence gets one evidence type: printed_edition, manuscript_reported_by (name the reporter), manuscript_inspected, in_manuscript_correction, later_quotation, emendation (with its stated grounds), translation, commentary_reading, lexicon, or project_inference. Never overwrite the printed text; an emendation is a branch. A later author's paraphrase or omission of a name is not a variant. In the eleven cases no manuscript was inspected directly, so every manuscript reading here is reported by someone else.

rules.title: List who holds a reading; do not count dependent sources as votes
rules.rule: Group sources by editorial project and by known copying. Record dependency as known, suspected or unknown, with the reason. For each branch, list holders by group. A translation reused from another passage cannot confirm a name in this one.

rules.title: Link parallel tellings, but do not import their people
rules.rule: Save a parallel_telling link between episodes, with a list of differences. A parallel can support a wording (it is evidence for a text reading). It does not fill an anonymous speaker, add a participant or prove that one event is meant. Different protagonists in parallel tellings are evidence about the traditions; keep them for a later identity or narrative pack. Do not write 'no evidence about either person', and do not merge.

rules.title: Source alternatives are not historical exclusivity
rules.rule: Keep the branch kinds apart: reported_alternative (the text itself says 'some say'), witness_variant, emendation, interpretation, segmentation. Within one reading a group may require exactly one choice. Whether the alternatives could all be historically true stays unknown by default and is a separate field. Allow nested branches (a variant inside an alternative) and explicit requires/excludes links between branches of different groups.

rules.title: Tag what a story is doing in a legal argument
rules.rule: Keep episode genre (halachic, aggadic, mixed, unknown) and add a function for a narrated unit that is cited: precedent, proof, illustration, attributed_precedent (inside someone's view), or personal_practice. Legal force belongs to the voice that states it. Later codifiers and commentators who generalise or reconstruct a story are later voices. Genre and function describe the text; they are not a probability that the event happened.

rules.title: Keep time claims with their voice and kind
rules.rule: Store a time claim with its voice and a kind: habitual, remembered_past, duration, relative_order, undated, or time_anchor (a biblical period used as a marker). Commentary dating of an event is a later voice. Calendar dates inside a legal rule are rule content, not event dates. Generation labels from commentators go into identity packs as biography proposals. Add no calendar dates.

rules.title: Confidence without invented numbers
rules.rule: Keep reading confidence as high/medium/low with its basis, holders and dependency groups. Keep identity and historical confidence empty in the passage reading. Record source hedges ('possible', 'apparently', 'probably') as hedges. Old pair-table probabilities stay as legacy data and are never shown as confidence. Commentary agreement is a basis label, not 'explicit'. A failed request or a search with no hits says nothing beyond its own scope.

rules.title: Build an evidence pack before any identity decision
rules.rule: An identity question opens a pack. The pack holds every local mention and its branch, name variants with evidence types, emendation grounds, parallel tellings, in-text identity statements, and outside biography claims with who made them. Its answer can be 'cannot tell'. A report inside the Talmud that 'it was not X but Y' is itself a source claim with a voice, not a decision.

proposed_changes.change: Entity kinds: add legal_role and household. Keep person, group, statement, event, place, object, work, unknown.
Claim field voice_kind with values anonymous_discussion, unattributed_opinion, named_speaker, nested_quote, later_author. Keep voice as the entity ID where there is one.
Replace basis with: explicit, name_internal, local_coreference, argued_in_text, self_described, commentary, translation, project_inference.
Speech claims: named roles speaker, addressee, audience, target, content. addressee may be absent. Remove the pilot habit of putting the target in object when no addressee is marked.

Statement fields: condition, outcome, count, scope (general/only/except), mood (plain/question/rhetorical), function (rule, precedent, proof, illustration, attributed_precedent, personal_practice), each allowed to vary by branch.

Two new predicates only: member_of_household (family family) and cites_statement (views family; statement to statement, with a function role: proof, objection, precedent, use). Everything else uncommon stays an event with the source verb and roles.

Reading groups: add kinds witness_variant, emendation, segmentation (keep reported_alternatives and interpretation_alternatives). Each branch gets evidence_type, held_by (source IDs), grounds, parent_branch, requires and excludes. Keep historical_compatibility separate and default unknown.
Source records: editorial_project, derived_from, dependency_status (known/suspected/unknown) with reason. Support summaries list holders by dependency group; no vote counts.
Constraint records: within_reading_exclusive, or conditional_incompatible with the identity hypothesis it depends on. No constraint deletes a branch.
Cross-passage records outside claims: parallel_telling (episodes, differences, which wording it supports) and in_text_identity_statement (voice, content).
Time claim kind: habitual, remembered_past, duration, relative_order, undated, time_anchor; always with voice.

Mechanical checks: every exact occurrence of listed names and pronouns has a mention; every patronymic has a parent entity and child_of claim; no inverse duplicates; every branch has evidence_type and held_by; every emendation has grounds; no numeric confidence fields; parent entity branch matches its name's branch; one mention per occurrence.

Two passes. Pass A reads only the base Hebrew or Aramaic and wider context, and marks what needs outside evidence. Pass B adds translations, commentaries and parallels as typed branches for the marked items only. Pass B never overwrites Pass A.

Automatic context growth: expand the window to the first mention when the text uses 'what is it?', a position label, an unresolved pronoun or 'Rav disagrees' without its object; record which segments were added.
Replace the three alternative kinds in the ontology with the five branch kinds of R12, and split 'witnesses differ' and 'readers differ' into the evidence types of R09.
Default view may hide non-acting parents, legal roles and later voices, but the data keeps them. Show derived labels (nephew, teacher of) with their path and the branch they depend on.

unresolved: No manuscript was inspected directly in any of the eleven cases. Every manuscript statement is reported by an editor or commentator.
The textual basis and mutual dependence of the Guggenheimer Hebrew, the Venice print and the Mechon-Mamre text were not checked.
What evidence should allow a 'fixed name or epithet' branch for a patronymic (Bar Qappara, original-08:dossier:F13) is not settled.
No criteria yet for when a parallel telling may support 'same event' rather than only 'same wording'.
member_of_household rests on two cases (challenge-30, random-yerushalmi-03). It needs more examples before its subtypes are fixed.
How far automatic context growth should go before it stops (challenge-30 needed 17a:9; random-bavli-03 needed 44b:11 and 45a:10; random-yerushalmi-04 needed 3:1:4).
Whether commentary agreement can ever justify high reading confidence when the commentaries' dependence is unknown (random-yerushalmi-01:dossier:PC4).
The eleven cases are now tuning material. They cannot measure the new rules; only held-out cases can.
random-bavli-05 and random-yerushalmi-06 were still in progress and are not reflected here.

procedure: Freeze the contract changes PC-A to PC-L and the reader changes PC-M and PC-N in a new run directory. Do not edit the frozen pilot.
Pass A on all held-out passages: base text plus wider context; mechanical mention inventory first.
Pass B only for items Pass A marks: add typed translation, commentary and parallel evidence with dependency groups.
Run the validator checks in PC-L. Keep failures visible per passage.
A separate reader checks each rule on each passage (pass, miss, not_applicable) without seeing expected outcomes for fresh random passages.
Report per rule: the case IDs where it failed, with the source words. No population accuracy.

per_rule_measures.R01: Patronymics in the inventory without parent entity or child_of claim.
